git add src/agent.py tests/test_voice_pipeline.py docs/model-selection.md VOICE_LATENCY_TEST_PLAN.md && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Upgrade LLM and TTS to verified LiveKit Inference ids; correct the latency plan

Separate commit from the transcript fix so it can be reverted on its own if
llm_ttft regresses on dev calls.

  LLM  openai/gpt-4.1-mini -> openai/gpt-4.1
  TTS  cartesia/sonic-3    -> cartesia/sonic-3.5
  STT  deepgram/flux-general-en (unchanged, id confirmed)

Ids were read verbatim from the LiveKit Inference model tables fetched as
raw markdown, not through a summarizer. The pinned SDK's `Literal` lists
are stale and enforce nothing — `inference.LLM(model: LLMModels | str)`
takes any string and validation happens at the gateway, on a live call —
so the docs are the only source of truth. They do not even list
deepgram/flux-general-en, which this branch already runs.

LLM: this model drives tool calls and every prohibition in the prompt, and
prod failures here have been instruction-following, not slowness (end_call
3s into the 2026-04-30 Goldman call; rogue DTMF the same day). Every
reasoning-tier model is disqualified on first-token latency: LiveKit's
gateway floors OpenAI reasoning_effort at "low" (no "minimal"), and Gemini
3's thinking_level is a plugin param, not an Inference one, so the tax
cannot be turned off. gemma-4-31b-it is LiveKit's recommended voice default
and is deliberately rejected — a 31B open-weight model optimizes the axis
we are not losing on. Traded: ~4x cost and some tokens/sec against mini,
for instruction-following, with no reasoning-token TTFT tax and no change
of provider family. Alternates sit beside each constant for a one-line A/B.

TTS: sonic-3.5 is what Cartesia's deprecated sonic-2/sonic-turbo migrate
to and has been served since 2026-05-04. sonic-3.6 shipped 2026-08-27, too
new to put in front of prod callers unreviewed; it is listed as an
alternate along with the frozen dated pin.

Endpointing, the question this branch opened: Flux does NOT double up with
the LiveKit turn detector, because c5c7fec already removed
MultilingualModel(). Confirmed in the SDK, not inferred —
audio_recognition.py:117 sets `self._turn_detector = turn_detection if not
isinstance(turn_detection, str) else None`, so `turn_detection="stt"` means
no EOU model object exists and the predict_end_of_turn branch never runs.
The bundled VAD stays, doing interruption detection, exactly as the
Deepgram page prescribes.

Consequence: max_endpointing_delay is now inert (only ever assigned inside
that turn-detector branch), so VOICE_LATENCY_TEST_PLAN.md was telling Ryan
to tune a variable that changes nothing — column removed.
min_endpointing_delay survives as a floor measured from last VAD speech,
not an addition to Flux's own wait, and at 0.5s it binds on every turn Flux
endpoints faster than that. Left at its default: it should move on measured
calls, not a code reading. EOUMetrics still fires under turn_detection=
"stt" (agent_activity.py:1563), so the plan stays runnable.

Verification:
  uv run pytest tests/ -q                 # 88 passed, 3 skipped
  uv run ruff format --check src/ tests/  # clean except pre-existing
                                          # tests/test_silence_monitor.py
  uv run ruff check src/agent.py          # 8 findings, all pre-existing at HEAD
Not verified — REQUIRED BEFORE MERGE: no call was placed and there are no
LiveKit credentials in this worktree, so "the docs list this id" is the
evidentiary ceiling. Run one dev call and confirm the Braintrust voice_call
span has non-empty latency_metrics_seconds.tts_ttfb (proves the TTS id AND
the voice= pairing were accepted; a rejected pairing means silent prod
calls) and non-empty llm_ttft. No deploy, no infra change from here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01FgCYhEXmVSDdy1YYnYY2NF
EOF
git log --oneline -3
